title: Settlement boundary expansion endorsed for county plan
subtitle: Well land purchases, telecom towers, speed limits, water use by-law, and a defeated Bissell Park reconsideration.
overview: Council endorsed staff's recommended settlement area boundary expansions and asked the County of Wellington to prepare the matching Official Plan amendment {{vote:m9}}. Several landowners' representatives asked for more land to be included or for a deferral. Staff said this is the start of the process, with more public input and a return to Council before the county adopts anything.

Council also approved two land purchases for future municipal supply wells, after a closed session {{vote:m3}}. It adopted a new outdoor water use by-law with tiered drought restrictions {{vote:m8}} and an updated speed by-law that lowers limits on several roads, with new signs promised by the end of the year {{vote:m7}}. Concurrence was given for two telecommunications towers. New branding, social media and hybrid meeting policies were adopted, along with a new procedure by-law.

A motion to waive notice and reconsider the October 15 Bissell Park multi-use pad decision was defeated {{vote:m16}}, so that earlier decision stands. The Mayor declared a conflict and left for that item. The meeting also recognized four lacrosse championship teams and heard a county update on new waste facility fees starting January 1, 2025.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the recommended expansions in Staff Report PLN2024-35 and asked the County of Wellington to draft the Official Plan amendment to implement them.
Council authorized purchase agreements for portions of land on Third Line West, Elora ($37,000) and Irvine Street, Salem ($92,500) for future municipal supply well facilities.
Council approved a new by-law regulating speed, repealing By-law 2023-85, and received an update on the 40 km/h neighbourhood pilot program.
Council approved a by-law promoting outdoor water conservation, with tiered restrictions tied to drought severity.
Council gave concurrence for a proposed 65 m self-supported telecommunications tower by SLI Towers at 7646 Colborne Street, Elora.
Council gave concurrence for a proposed 25 m Rogers monopole tower at 800-840 Tower Street South, Fergus.
Council authorized a new Procedure By-law replacing By-law 2021-31 and directed staff to prepare a 2025 meeting schedule.
A motion to waive notice and rescind the October 15 decision on the Bissell Park refrigerated multi-use pad was defeated, so that decision stands.

debate: Delegates for several landowners argued their sites were well suited to growth and already close to services, and asked Council to include them or defer the decision. One cited newer Ministry of Finance population forecasts and warned of returning to the issue soon.

Staff replied that more land meets the criteria than the identified need, that the county forecasts can still be used under the new provincial policy, and that the amendment process allows further public input and returns to Council.

On the procedure by-law, one councillor objected to a longer meeting curfew, citing barriers to participation, and proposed keeping the current curfew. Another preferred keeping delegations at 10 minutes. The clerk suggested a five-minute default with extensions.

On speed limits, councillors asked about enforcement and further 40 km/h areas. Staff said they coordinate with the OPP each spring and will bring more neighbourhood recommendations with next April's annual report.

On Bissell Park, a point of order questioned whether the reconsideration motion complied with the procedure by-law. The chair ruled it in order, and the ruling was upheld on appeal. Some councillors opposed waiving the notice requirement as setting a precedent, and one said a covered refrigerated pad would have been preferable.
